text:
alex.kim: Kicking off a Q2 runtime perf prioritization thread. Need to agree on scope for kernels, quant, KV cache, and launch criteria for the throughput/latency OKR. TL;DR: customers asking lower p99 and 2x throughput for batching workloads.

maya.patel: +1. Sales flagged 3 enterprise accounts wanting p99 < 120ms for 4k tokens in low-burst windows. Also one customer needs deterministic KV TTL behavior.

sam: Can we break into must-have vs nice-to-have? My rough split: (A) kernel micro-optimizations + KV cache primitives (must), (B) 4-bit quant research + compilation improvements (high), (C) auto-batching policy UI (medium).

jordan: From model side: 4-bit quant helps memory but may regress quality on some opt checkpoints. We need a small eval suite per customer to gate rollout. Suggest include automatic fallback to fp16 for flagged prompts.

nina.chen: Operational constraints: Dedicated clusters have different perf profiles. If we push aggressive batching, SRE needs a safety throttle to avoid latency tail spikes. Can we define max batch latency budget?

tori: For OKRs we stated: "Improve host inference throughput by 2x and reduce p99 latency by 30% for common gen workloads." We should map features to measurable rollouts (canary -> stage -> prod) and acceptance criteria.

sam: Proposal for acceptance criteria: 
```
- End-to-end p50/p95/p99 measured on our benchmark harness
- No quality regression > 2% on customer eval sets
- CPU/GPU utilization within target thresholds
- KV hit-rate >= 80% for configured TTLs
```

maya.patel: That looks reasonable. Add cost delta threshold: unit token cost shouldn't increase > 10% for hosted tier. Customers will push back otherwise.

alex.kim: Good call. Now about kernels: do we prioritize fused attention kernels (gains for long seq) or matmul tiling improvements (general gains)? Sam, what's highest ROI?

sam: Fused attention yields biggest win for long sequences (>2k), matmul tiling helps short/medium. Given customer mix (many 1k-3k), fused attention first. We can land a subset of kernels in 6 weeks with perf tests.

jordan: Parallel work: quant-aware kernel selection in compiler. If we land fused attention first, we need matching kernels for 4-bit paths to avoid falling back to slower execution.

nina.chen: Can we quantify rollout risk? If a kernel change causes an OOM on some Dedicated configs, we need instant rollback. Suggest feature-flag + ephemeral canary with strict mem checks.

tori: Timeline ask from product/sales: demo-ready in 8 weeks for enterprise briefing. Is that realistic?

sam: 8 weeks for a demo (canary + perf slides) is plausible if we scope to fused attention + KV cache TTL consistency + canary infra. 4-bit quant can be staged after demo.

maya.patel: I'll tell sales to set expectations: demo focusing on latency/throughput improvements, not final quantized models. Also we'll require sign-off on quality evals before any customer-facing quant rollout.

alex.kim: OKRs mapping action items: 
- Kernel: fused attention landing (owner: sam) — acceptance: p99 improvement >= 20% on long-seq bench
- KV: native TTL and consistent hits (owner: nina) — acceptance: hit-rate >= 80% and deterministic evictions in canary
- Canary infra: feature flag + instant rollback (owner: eng-infra / deploy-bot) — acceptance: automatic rollback < 5m on failure
- Quant: 4-bit research + eval harness (owner: jordan) — acceptance: quality regressions <= 2% on customer evals
- Cost guardrails (owner: tori/maya) — acceptance: unit cost delta <= 10%

deploy-bot: scheduled canary cluster creation: canary-rt-2026-05-06T14:00Z (ETA 6d). Will post updates.

nina.chen: I'll add automated mem/latency checks to the canary job. Also adding an alert if p99 increases by >10% vs baseline.

sam: I'll open RFC with kernel plan and bench scripts today, link back here. Expect initial PRs in 1 week.

maya.patel: Thanks. I'll compile this into a one-pager for GTM and customer comms.

alex.kim: Great. Final quick Q: any blockers that would prevent demo in 8 weeks? Call them out now.

jordan: Main blocker: model eval tooling for customer-specific prompts. Need help from devex to collect labeled sets.
tori: I'll coordinate with devex.

alex.kim: Perfect. We'll reconvene in 5 business days with RFC + canary infra checklist. :thumbsup:
